title: A Primitive can be globally Active with zero Instances, so Active means enabled rather than in use
content:
Three Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives in the Osero Artifact all carry Global Activation Status `Active`, but they are not in the same condition. Distribution Reward (A.6.1.1.7.2.5.1.1.1) and Integration Boost (A.6.1.1.7.2.5.2.1.1) have `Active` status with no Instance Configuration Document Location under their Active Instances Directory — nothing has been invoked. Pioneer Chain (A.6.1.1.7.2.5.3.1.1) has `Active` status and a live Plasma Instance.

The three-way comparison fixes the semantics. Global Activation Status describes whether the Agent may use the Primitive at all, not whether it currently does. `Inactive` — as on the Token SkyLink and Light Agent Primitives — means the door is shut; `Active` means the door is open, whether or not anyone has walked through.

That separation is what makes the directory structure informative. Capability and usage are tracked on different axes: the Hub status answers "is this permitted," the Instance directories answer "is this happening." Reading only one gives a wrong picture of an Agent — an Agent with many `Active` Primitives may be doing nothing with most of them.

For Osero specifically it means the demand-side toolkit is provisioned ahead of use: two of three reward mechanisms are switched on and waiting, which is a statement of intent rather than of activity.
description: Osero's Distribution Reward and Integration Boost Primitives are both `Active` with empty directories, while Pioneer Chain is `Active` with a live Instance — the status marks availability.
